entityName: University of Tras-os-Montes e Alto Douro
entityDescription: UTAD is organized in 5 Schools: Agricultural and Veterinary Sciences, Social and Human Sciences, Sciences and Technology, Life Sciences and Environment and the Nursing School. The permanent teaching staff of 530 teachers (393 with PhD) and 522 technical and administrative staff support about 8000 students. UTAD offers 37 graduate courses (1st cycle) and about 77 2nd cycle and PhD courses. Research activities are concentrated in 8 Research Centres: Centre for Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Centre for Research and Technology of Agro-Environment and Biological Sciences, Centre for Development and Transdisciplinary Studies, Centre for Studies in the Letters, Centre for Chemistry, Centre of Mathematic Studies, and the Centre for Sports, Health and Human Development. The Research Units have duplicated the scientific production of “refereed” papers of the SCI during the last 3 years. Research Units accommodate researchers from other institutions in Portugal and abroad. A gradual increase in the link to stakeholders and SME’s has been achieved, as well as an increase in the number of scholarships. UTAD has a wide portfolio of projects (financed nationally and internationally) with high activity and relevance in all the areas, but more action is necessary in the H2020, although several proposals have been submitted. The University of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro-UTAD has a wide experience in project management, both national and international, framed in various types of financing programs. In national projects funded stand out Foundation for Science and Technology-FCT (more than 100 projects), Compete, Innovation Agency, ON.2 and Proder. Regarding to Innovation, Technology Transfer and University-Industry cooperation, UTAD have an Industrial Liaison Office, working also as TTO, to support the cooperation with industry and the technology transfer. In terms of technology transfer projects, this office as, at the moment, for national projects. We are also member of some international networks. In terms of international projects UTAD has participated in European projects (FP6 and FP7) and has had a strong involvement in projects of the INTERREG program, including the INTERREG IIIA, IIIB, IVB and POCTEP SUDOE either as promoter or as a partner entity. The results obtained with the various projects and partnerships allow us to ensure our competence and experience in the interaction with various partners and actors in the management and monitoring of large projects.

entityDescription:
The University of Valladolid is one of the most important centers of Higher Education in Spain. It counts on four campuses -Valladolid, Palencia, Segovia and Soria, over 100 degrees, 80 doctoral programs (14 with Honor Mention) and 68 postgraduate degree, accredited international relations and prestigious research Centers. On average, nearly 25,000 students enroll each year, counts on more than 2,500 teachers and nearly 1,000 people dealing with administration tasks and other services. Over 60% of students do internships in companies and other institutions. It offers a comprehensive range of double international degrees, and promotes the transfer of research results. 
The UVA has 300 km2 for researching activities, 5 buildings devoted exclusively to research, 4 Certified Laboratories Industry serving nearly 300 research laboratories, 19 research institutes and all departments needed. A landmark Lab-building (foundation 2014), called LUCIA (0% CO2 emissions; 0% energy consumption, with LEED Platinum certification and Green Certification), with 2,100 m2 for researching related to efficiency energy buildings and agrofood (nutrition, food and dietary laboratories). 
The UVA manages around 180/year research projects financed through competitive public R+D+i calls (European, national or regional), and approximately 500 contracts and agreements aimed at the transfer of knowledge and technology, amounting to an average value of over fifteen million Euros per annum. Moreover, its researchers take part in almost 250 further projects and contracts managed by other institutions.
UVA has been taking part in a very active way in different European projects, at research or training level, during the last 20 years. There is a long experience in international projects developed by different groups of research in the University and different fields of knowledge.

entityDescription: Tallysman designs and manufactures antennas for Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for a wide range of applications including: precision agriculture; asset tracking and performance; geodetics; timing; marine, autonomous vehicles; sports performance and personal tracking; and satellite communications. The corporation also designs and manufactures GNSS utility systems and software that enhance the functionality of two-way mobile radio systems (Motorola, Tait, and Kenwood). Incorporated in 2009, Tallysman Wireless Inc. is located at Kanata, Ontario, Canada where all R&D and manufacturing operations occur. When Tallysman was founded, the principals focused on the design and manufacturing of GNSS antennas with enhanced performance for the evolving GNSS environment. This included GPS and the then-renewed GLONASS system, plus the Galileo and Beidou systems then under development in Europe and China, respectively. This required antennas with wider bandwidth, a truly circular response through a much wider bandwidth, and better multipath rejection. The over-arching objective is to improve the precision of GNSS systems by providing cleaner signals to the receiver; free of multi-path or cross-polarized signals. Thus, Tallysman developed the dual feed antenna architecture (which we branded as Accutenna�). This technology has proven its ability to substantially increase the rejection of multi-path signals leading to increased accuracy of position by the system. Tallysman has also developed an antenna technology enabling high precision for geodetic/reference applications (which we branded as Veraphase�). Tallysman continues to develop new products to fit the ever-changing needs and applications of the market.

NTE-SENER is the new name of the former company NTE after the purchase of NTE by SENER Ingeniería y Sistemas. 

Since 1987, NTE-SENER has been providing engineering services for the development of custom, high-performance systems, instruments and equipment for advanced research and applications. Its original focus on solutions for the Life Sciences and Biomedical sectors has evolved to cover needs in other scientific domains as well. Nowadays, NTE-SENER meets needs in markets with demanding requirements and specific processes and regulations such as space, science, healthcare and industry. 

NTE-SENER positions itself as a ¿systems¿ company, internationally oriented and focused on niche segments within the markets where it operates. The company¿s multidisciplinary engineering skills and capabilities are focused on the following product lines: 


- Instrumentation for space science, microgravity and life support 
- Payloads electronics 
- Precision mechatronics for optical and electro-optical devices 
- Bio-engineering systems and bio-medical devices 

The company¿s business is devoted to the development of custom instruments, systems and equipment for advanced research and applications mainly in life and physical sciences, with outstanding presence and performance in the space, scientific research and bio-medical markets. 

NTE-SENER¿s services and products address the needs of research organizations, technological institutes and industrial companies which require high added-value engineering development services. Its activities range from feasibility and systems studies to the production of hardware prototypes (including short-series) and software systems. 

NTE-SENER runs a corporate quality system which is ISO 9001:2008-certified and which enables the company to operate in markets where project, process and quality management are critical.

entityDescription:
BREDEX GmbH has 30 years’ experience in delivering tailor-made solutions. Based in Braunschweig, we employ around 75 developers, who work in dynamic teams on individual customer projects. Our expertise in software development makes us branch-independent – last year for example we worked on mobile applications for the automotive industry, as well as a web portal for a large company group. Our “Wünsch dir eine app” campaign, where we sponsored the development of an app for a charity, was particularly interesting for the media.

Alongside our software development activities, we are well known for the Open Source testing tool Jubula and our testing competence. BREDEX has a team of test consultants who support internal and external projects, and we are present at various testing conferences to share our experiences. 

Conferences aren’t the only place where we share our knowledge. BREDEX offers seminars in mobile testing and is a certified ISQI partner for the CMAP® certification. We also organize special training courses, for example our Java Boot Camp. We designed this course for an automotive customer in 2015 as a way to teach a non-IT audience about IT and software development using Lego Mindstorms®. It has been held successfully multiple times since. 

Since 2015, we have also increased our technological knowledge to include interaction design and augmented reality. At the CeBIT 2016, we presented applications and prototypes relevant to mobile business cases using these new areas. 

Regardless of the project, we value quality at all stages of the development process, as well as close contact and communication with our customers. We prefer lean, agile processes to ensure customer satisfaction, and we implement continuous testing and integration to provide quick feedback. We use a wide variety of modern technologies for our projects while remaining true to our roots of being platform- and manufacturer-independent. BREDEX is active in the Open Source community as a Solutions Member of the Eclipse Foundation.

entityDescription:
De Montfort University (DMU) is a dynamic institution with a long and vibrant history of improving people’s lives through education.

Originally founded as the Leicester School of Art in 1870, the university has evolved through many incarnations including the Leicester Colleges of Art and Technology and Leicester Polytechnic.

Leicester Polytechnic officially became De Montfort University on 26 June 1992. The name was chosen to reflect the University’s long association with Leicester by commemorating the celebrated Simon de Montfort, Earl of Leicester, a crucial figure in medieval history who established the first parliament in 1265.

Our reputation for quality and distinctiveness in teaching and research is a direct result of our heritage. Many modern DMU courses have their roots in the late 19th century and early 20th century, when the School of Art and Leicester Technical School began training apprentices for local industries such as boot and shoe manufacture, furniture making and design, hosiery and textiles manufacture, engineering, printing and book binding.

Art, pharmacy, corsetry, footwear, physical sciences and architecture were taught at the Schools and are still in evidence at DMU today, either as courses in their own right, or as integral components of more modern courses.

A commitment to ensuring teaching kept pace with the changing needs of businesses meant that computing courses were introduced in the 1960s; DMU’s computing degrees are still highly valued by industry.

The university has grown and evolved over the years, but it is still dedicated to providing inspirational teaching to students and it has a significant impact on the world around it.

Nuclear NDT Research & Services, Ltd. was founded at the beginning of 2000 to target primarily customers from the nuclear power industry, and is working now for all important industrial sectors (energy – nuclear and classic, heavy industry, aerospace industry, chemical, oil refinery etc.). With engineering groups, laboratories, and qualified personnel for nondestructive examinations, materials testing and modeling of thermo-mechanical behavior, we are focused to give complete answers for Structural Integrity Inspection, Remaining Life Evaluation, and Failure Prevention. 

The Quality Management System of Nuclear NDT Research & Services is certified according to SR EN ISO 9001: 2008, and is authorized by the Romanian Authority for the Control and Approval of Boilers, Pressure Vessels and Hoisting Equipment (ISCIR) and by the National Commission for Nuclear Activities Control (CNCAN). Our destructive and nondestructive laboratories are accreditated according to SR EN ISO/CEI 17025/2005.

entityDescription:
Fera, works collaboratively with the private sector, and public bodies - both locally and internationally. Our role is to innovate and develop good, translational science that will protect and enhance food, plant, animal and environmental quality. Our vision is to be a leading supplier of scientific solutions, evidence and advice across the agri-food supply chain. Our role is about understanding problems and enabling sustainable solutions through innovative thinking and the gathering and analysis of robust scientific evidence. This gives us the right platform to be able to support our customers in both the strategic and day-to-day decisions they face. Fera at a glance • We have a scientific heritage of over 100 years • We have over 7,500 government and commercial customers • We run over 600 research projects per year • We provide services to customers in over 100 countries • We analyse over 100,000 samples a year • We have over 100 procedures accredited to ISO 17025 • We work with more than 1,000 collaboration partners • We employ over 350 scientists and technical specialists including over 70 with PhDs • We are the National Reference Laboratory in 9 different areas • In a typical year our work leads to the publication of over 100 peer reviewed papers listed in the Science Citation Index 

Note: The legal address of our company is 65 gresham street, the actual trading address of our company is york biotech campus sand hutton york
